bossAlertStep: Drag the move handle to reposition the panel vertically or horizontally, and choose the compact size in Manage. The × hides the panel; sound and browser notifications continue according to your settings. Reopen it from My boss alerts on the Field bosses page.
characterRankingNote: Character search shows rankings only when the owner has agreed to make the name public. A private name and a public character with no rankings have separate messages. Check the weekly and all-time periods separately.
photoNote: Character backgrounds are shared across all presets on this PC. Backups can include the selection, framing and character assignments of built-in photos. Personal photo files and their settings are excluded from backup and restore.
sourceNote: NotMeter 1.0.308 · October 31, 2026. Settings and records were captured with the current app renderer. Characters and values are examples. Unchanged display examples may use earlier captures.
languageNote: Instructions are available in 10 languages. Vietnamese keeps game terms in English and uses English app screenshots.
startStep: At first launch, choose your language and sharing preferences in Privacy choices before starting. All choices are optional: leave everything unchecked and select Start without agreeing to use the meter without sharing. Your choices are saved on this PC.
languageStep: Vietnamese translates general instructions while keeping game terms, including skills, items and classes, in English.

Pvp: PvP meter and statistics
Open Settings → PvP encounter analysis, choose your options, then save.

Enable PvP collection, which is OFF by default. Only encounters observed after enabling it can be collected. Enable PvP rows to let the main meter switch to opponents automatically. An ongoing PvE fight takes display priority.
Click an opponent row for their analysis. You can also open analysis using the meter’s PvP button or the tray menu. Hover over the meter to reveal its controls.
Attack statistics show hits you deal; defense statistics show hits you receive. Select the hit statistics and DPS you want to display, and check which direction you are viewing.

Exclude guaranteed critical skills and exclude forced block/evade are ON by default. Confirmed guaranteed effects are removed from the relevant rate’s numerator and denominator; damage and total hit counts stay unchanged. Perfect hits and perfect blocks are different metrics.
Set 1–10 opponents, 75–150% row size and 20–100% opacity. Higher opacity means a more solid background. Check the settings preview, then save. PvE opacity is separate.

Choose a base sort: recent encounter, damage dealt or damage taken. Important-opponent priority defaults to Off. Recent target prioritizes the opponent you directly attacked within 10 seconds; damage over time and summon attacks do not change that target.

Low health prioritizes the lowest remaining HP percentage confirmed within 5 seconds. Unknown HP follows known values; defeated opponents come last. Priority ordering changes at most once a second, while damage and HP keep updating.
Remaining HP appears as a gauge and disappears at zero. Missing observations or unknown maximum HP are not estimated. A missing gauge does not necessarily mean the opponent is dead.

Hourly kills/assists combines kills and assists per opponent. It resets at each full hour and continues showing the observed count beyond the 3-kill reference. PvP daily points use the same history and time settings as the regular point display.
You can select the minimum Abyss rank to show and collect under Settings → PvP combat analysis.
Selecting “1-Star Officer and above” includes every rank from 1-Star Officer through Supreme Commander and excludes Trainee and all soldier ranks.
The default is “Show and collect all”. When a rank filter is enabled, opponents with unknown ranks are excluded until their rank is identified.
Saved history is preserved, and your chosen setting is kept after restarting the app.
Confirmed Abyss ranks appear beside opponents’ names, for example [ Supreme Commander ].
You can toggle this display in Settings. It is ON by default.
Added “Combat row text size” to Settings → PvP combat analysis. The default is 100%, with an adjustable range of 80–150%.
Changing the text size preserves the window size, existing three-column layout, and displayed information.
Long character names and localized text scale only as far as the available space allows, preventing clipping and overlap.
PvP encounter tracking and combat row display stop when you enter Abyss Outland.
Tracking resumes from the next encounter after returning to a regular PvP area, according to your existing settings.
PvP is still in development. It shows observed data; kill/assist counts may differ from the game’s reward decisions. Send feedback through Discord.

Minimum rank controls which new opponents are displayed and collected; the rank beside a name is a separate label. Hiding the label does not disable the rank filter. Choose Show/collect all to include opponents whose rank is unknown.
After saving, check opponent rows, attack/defense mode, selected metrics and sorting during PvP.
pvpHistory: Hiding a row does not reset its damage totals.

In Settings → PvP encounter analysis, inactive-row hiding defaults to 60 seconds and supports 10–600 seconds. Hiding defeated opponents is ON by default, with a 10-second delay adjustable from 1–120 seconds.

To count a new fight from zero, reset the current encounter or enable automatic encounter reset with a 10–600 second delay. Automatic reset is OFF by default. You can also use the meter’s reset hotkey.
The × on a row hides only that opponent; Restore manually hidden rows brings it back. The top × disables PvP rows while collection continues. With no visible rows, the meter returns to its idle view.
Choose an encounter in saved history, then click an opponent and skill to inspect details. Saved encounters survive resets, zone changes, collection OFF and app restarts.
History settings keep 10–500 recent encounters, with a default of 100. The oldest unpinned records are removed when the limit is exceeded. Pin records you want to keep until you delete them.
Use the controls at the bottom right of the analysis window to adjust text size from 80% to 150% in 10% steps.
The default is 100%, matching the previous size. Click the percentage button to restore the default.
The setting applies to both live engagement analysis and archived records. Statistics layout and text wrapping adapt to larger text.
Buffs and effects observed on your opponent during an encounter are shown with their icons, names, active durations, and uptime percentages.
Uptime is calculated over the interval from the first hit to the last hit. Overlapping periods of the same effect are not counted twice.
The limit counts encounters, not opponents. History stays on this PC and is not transferred by settings backup codes. Detail-window size is restored when you reopen it.
Open a saved encounter and its skill details, then pin any records you want to keep.
privacyChoices: Combat sharing, public character names and daily usage statistics are separate choices.
Choose a language at the top of Privacy choices. Review combat statistics sharing, publishing all your characters detected on this PC, and daily usage statistics separately.
Agree to all and start enables all three. To share only selected information, start with your selections. To decline everything, clear all boxes and choose Start without agreeing.

Allowing public names on this PC applies to your characters detected afterwards. It does not grant consent for other players. Players who have not agreed appear as *** in public rankings and combat details, including Global.

Your choices are stored on this PC and can be changed in Settings. You are not asked again for each character detection. Importing a settings backup or share code on another PC does not restore consent.

If the kill/attempt history shows a public-name/upload notice, read it before using its button. That button enables both character publicity and record uploads. Check the record’s status separately for eligibility and server registration.
Open Kill / Attempt History → Show name in rankings to check the current character’s visibility. Choose ‘Hide ranking name’ in that window to withdraw consent for this character.
In Settings → General, turning OFF consent to show all your characters’ names requests withdrawal for characters managed on this PC.

Characters whose consent was withdrawn individually stay private when you turn the all-characters option back ON. To make one public again, wait for that character to be detected and give consent in its individual visibility window.
You can use the meter without agreeing. Enabling sharing does not guarantee that every record immediately appears in rankings.

Consent and withdrawal appear on the website in the next statistics publication after server processing, so the change may not be immediate. Hiding a name does not delete existing combat records; request record deletion separately.
Review your saved choices and distinguish saved, sent and registered record states.
menuVisibility: Hide while game menus are open
An optional feature that temporarily hides the meter in game menus. Default: OFF.
Enable automatic hiding in game menus under Settings → General and save. The meter returns after supported menus such as inventory or map close. AION1 control mode is supported.
Keep visible during combat defaults to ON and only affects menu hiding when that feature is enabled. It prevents menu detection from hiding the meter during combat.
Combat-only display, hide during combat, manual visibility and game-only display still apply. Keeping visible during combat does not force the meter over those other settings.
Party lookup and the OBS browser source are excluded from menu hiding. A brief recovery delay can occur while rapid menu changes settle.
Added an ON/OFF option for the hide/show fade animation under Settings → General.
The default is ON. It applies when hiding or showing the meter with a shortcut or other controls, and when game menu detection hides or shows it automatically.
Set it to OFF to hide or show the meter immediately without animation.
If unwanted hiding repeats, turn this feature OFF and report the menu, rendering mode and a screenshot.
Check opening/closing menus and combat visibility; party lookup should remain available.
healing: Choose healing per second and accumulated healing separately.
Under Settings → Meter → Display, enable HPS and/or total healing. Total healing is OFF by default and independent of total damage.
Choose which classes to show, self-only, hide zero healing and the healing color. Check the preview and save.
HPS is healing you cast divided by combat duration; total healing is the sum of that healing. Healing received from other players is not added to your own healing output.
When total damage is also enabled, both values share the same area. Backup/share codes carry the display settings, not the actual healing records.
Damage and healing are different metrics. HPS is a rate; total healing is an accumulated amount.
Check the selected characters in a fight where healing occurs.
dailyPoints: Review today’s gains separately from gains during each hour.
Click the meter’s daily-points area, then open its settings. If the area is hidden, enable daily points under Meter → Display.
Reset every hour shows gains from each full hour. Also show today’s total adds the daily amount in parentheses: this hour (today). This option requires hourly reset.
Choose the reset-time region, check the displayed clock and next reset, then save. Daylight saving is handled automatically; existing alert settings do not change.
Hourly history shows Abyss Points and Ranking Points by date and hour. History is kept whether hourly display reset is ON or OFF.
Daily totals start at 05:00 in the character’s server time. Time while NotMeter is off is not reconstructed. The PvP points display shares this history and time setting.
When display is turned OFF and back ON, subsequent gains are counted from the most recently confirmed balance. Points gained while display was OFF are not added retroactively.
Period history and hunting-efficiency views remain available. Resetting the display does not delete history. An unobserved value shown as — is not zero.

Today's total starts at 05:00 in the character's server time. A selected date in hourly history instead covers 00:00–24:00 in your chosen time zone. Match the time ranges before comparing totals, because the day boundaries differ.
Check the selected region’s clock, next reset and the period used for the displayed total.
Render: Auto, GPU, CPU and Rust rendering
Choose the rendering mode that is stable on your PC.
Settings → Rendering offers Auto, GPU preferred, Compatibility (CPU) and Rust · GPUI (D3D11). If your display works well, keep Auto or your current mode.
Rust is a separate experimental GPU renderer. Try it when comparing CPU load or stuttering with existing GPU/CPU modes. Save and restart NotMeter to apply the change fully.
Check combat, scrolling/resizing details, settings, dragging, returning from Alt-Tab and alerts. Rust does not guarantee higher FPS or AFMF compatibility.

RTSS output is a separate feature, not another name for Rust. Read the RTSS guide before using it. If performance or display problems occur, disable the affected output/experimental option and return to a stable mode.
If text looks blurry, compare Sharp and Smooth text rendering in meter design settings, then save. Also check font size and Windows scaling.
If the entire monitor repeatedly turns black or flickers severely, check whether closing NotMeter stops it and report GPU, driver, rendering mode and RTSS use.
After restarting, check the saved mode, returning to the game, dragging and detail windows.
Backup: Back up settings and restore on another PC
Choose what to export and what to import separately.
Open Settings → Backup/restore → Back up and select the relevant sections. Include Combat assist for skills/buffs/cooldowns, Alerts for sound/schedules, and Hotkeys for key bindings.
Create a code and copy it or save it to a file. Generate a new code after changing settings; an old code does not update itself.
On the other PC, use the latest NotMeter and paste the complete code into Restore, then review its contents. Current backups, older full backups and older design codes use the same screen.
Review the separate caution settings. Visibility rules, alerts and hotkeys default to Keep my settings. Explicitly choose Import for what you want to restore, then apply the selected settings.
Built-in meter photos can be restored when their photo section is included. Personal image files are excluded and must be selected again on the new PC.
Recheck combat-assist skills/buffs/cooldowns, alerts, hotkeys and party lookup. Restoration saves immediately. Window positions, current lock state and PC-specific network settings stay unchanged.
Consent, credentials, personal image files and actual combat-history files are excluded. Importing another user’s shared settings does not automatically enable PvP collection.
Reopen Settings to check the restored values, then try a skill or alert.
assistBars: Bar theme and buff gauges
Track buff duration on the bar and cooldown inside the icon at the same time.
First turn ON Show Combat Assist UI at the top. In Skills, enable buff display and cooldown display for the skill you want, then choose Buffs + cooldowns as the display mode in Appearance.
You can select the “Bars · Buff + Cooldown” theme under Settings → Combat Assist UI.
Buff duration is shown as a bar and a number, while the cooldown appears inside the skill icon, so you can track both at once.
The icon’s teal gauge and its boundary move downward as the cooldown counts down, with the remaining seconds shown in the center.
When the cooldown ends, the gauge and number disappear. They update when you use the skill again.
Choose from five gauge designs, with “Contrast fill” as the default.
Under Settings → Combat Assist UI → Appearance & layout, you can adjust bar width, bar height, and timer text size independently. Enlarging the numbers does not enlarge the entire bar.
Set separate normal, warning, and near-expiry colors for the gauge and timer text.
Added gauge visibility and a black outline for timer numbers to improve readability against bright backgrounds.
Long timer values, skill names, and party member names shrink to fit the available space, preventing clipping and overlap.
Added separate “Cooldown numbers on icons” and “Cooldown gauges on icons” options under Settings → Combat Assist UI → Appearance.
Numbers and gauges can be turned ON/OFF independently, including in the long-cooldown compact mode.
Both options default to ON. If the previous combined option was OFF, both remain OFF.
Numbers continue to update with the remaining time even when the gauge is hidden. The adjacent buff timers and bars, existing size and layout, cooldown tracking and alerts are preserved.
Under Settings → Combat Assist UI → Appearance, you can adjust the timer's X position in the timer-first style.
The range is 0–80px, with a default of 0px. The timer stays vertically centered and is positioned to avoid overlapping skill names.
When ‘Show only when buffs/cooldowns exist’ is ON, empty circular gauges are hidden for skills without an active buff.
The gauge appears when a buff starts and hides again when it ends. Always-visible icons and your existing layout are preserved.
When the option is OFF, the empty circular outline remains visible as before.
Added a “Hide skill names” ON/OFF option under Settings → Combat Assist UI → Appearance.
The default is OFF. Turning it on hides only skill names; buff bars, remaining time, icon cooldowns, and stack counts stay visible.

When finished, click Save at the bottom right. After your character is detected in game, use the selected skill or receive its buff to check the live display. Preview numbers are sample values, not a live fight.
The five gauge designs change the buff display. They are separate from the cooldown inside the icon. Hide skill names defaults to OFF.

Color changes use the buff’s remaining duration, independently of cooldown-ready and buff-end alert timing. If nothing appears, check Combat Assist ON, selected skills, display mode and the combat-only visibility condition in that order.
Save, then check that the same skill shows both a buff bar and icon cooldown, and that colors change at your warning thresholds.
assistCompact: Group long cooldowns into small icons while keeping important skills expanded.
You can configure compact display for long cooldowns under Settings → Combat Assist UI → Appearance. The default is OFF.
Skills with only a cooldown remaining and no active buff are grouped as small icons. The default threshold is 10 seconds or more remaining.
You can change the threshold. Skills expand back into bars when their remaining cooldown falls below it. Skills with an active buff are never compacted.
Set the threshold from 1 to 600 seconds. Use the skill selection button under compact exclusions to open the larger picker. It lists supported skills with self or party cooldown display enabled.
Narrow the list by skill or class search, class filter, or Selected only. Check your choices, apply them, then save in Settings. Cancel discards changes made in the picker.
Numbers and gauges can be turned ON/OFF independently, including in the long-cooldown compact mode.
Both options default to ON. If the previous combined option was OFF, both remain OFF.
Numbers continue to update with the remaining time even when the gauge is hidden. The adjacent buff timers and bars, existing size and layout, cooldown tracking and alerts are preserved.
Skills with an active buff never compact. This changes the display, not the skill’s actual cooldown.

This applies only to the bar theme. If a skill stays expanded, check that compact mode is ON, no buff is active, the cooldown meets the threshold and the skill is not excluded. If the exclusion list is empty, first enable cooldown display for a supported skill in Skills.
Check that only skills without an active buff compact and that they expand below the threshold. Excluded skills must stay as bars during long cooldowns.
assistVoice: Custom start and end voice phrases
Choose what is spoken after the skill name and preview the actual announcement.

For sound only, set Popup OFF, Sound ON and Voice OFF for that event. Enable the common sound in Alerts & voice and check its volume. A popup is not required. Under Skill sounds & volume, keep common settings or choose a separate sound and volume.

Set popup, sound and voice independently for cooldowns, buff starts and buff ends. Choose common or individual timing and hover over the bulbs for details. Skill selection has no bottom live preview; check the display in Appearance & layout, then save. Existing backup and share-code settings are preserved.
Speaks skill alerts using your selected reading style. Voice works without popups or sound effects. Set the voice and reading style in Alerts & voice.
Set separate start and end phrases under Settings → Combat Assist UI → Alerts & voice. Announcements read “skill name + your phrase”.
Phrases can contain up to 40 characters. The voice preview lets you hear the actual announcement.

Keeping the default phrases preserves the existing announcements. A blank start phrase also uses the default. Changing a phrase does not enable voice alerts: check the skill’s start and end voice toggles too.
Skill name only omits the phrase and time. Choose another announcement style to hear your phrase, and decide whether to read the remaining time aloud.
Listen works even with voice alerts OFF. For announcements in combat, enable both global voice under Alerts & voice and the skill’s start/end voice switches, set voice volume above zero, then save.
Start and end phrases each support up to 40 characters. Your phrase is not automatically changed to “Buff end”.
Enable that skill’s start and end voice alerts, preview the phrase and remaining time, then save.
assistSkills: Skill buffs and stacks
Enable supported options in Skills and check the buff when it activates.

Open Settings → Combat Assist UI → Skill selection. Choose Class skills, Party buffs, Party cooldowns, Boss debuffs, or Common & consumables. You can configure other classes’ buffs as well as your own class skills.

Find a skill with the name search and class filter, then select it on the left. Set buff/cooldown visibility and always-show options on the right. Party buffs are effects another character applies to you; party cooldowns track readiness per caster. Select your own cooldowns separately.

Set popup, sound and voice independently for cooldowns, buff starts and buff ends. Choose common or individual timing and hover over the bulbs for details. Skill selection has no bottom live preview; check the display in Appearance & layout, then save. Existing backup and share-code settings are preserved.
Added Cleric's Chain of Torment debuff tracking to Combat Assist UI: Supported on Korean, Taiwanese and Global servers.
Available under Settings → Combat Assist UI → Skills → Boss Debuff. The default is OFF.
Shows the debuff's remaining duration on the target and updates when it is reapplied, refreshed or removed.
Added Templar’s Block Pain to Combat Assist UI: Configure its display under Settings → Combat Assist UI → Skills → Templar. The default is OFF.
Shows the remaining duration of Block Pain when it activates after taking a hit, and updates when the buff activates again, its duration refreshes, or it is removed.
You can configure always-on buff display, start and end alerts, and voice announcements. It works with the existing Combat Assist UI themes.
You can enable Elemental Fusion under Settings → Combat Assist UI → Skills → Spiritmaster.
A disabled gray switch is unavailable for that skill. Buff display, popup alerts and voice are separate choices: enabling the display does not automatically enable voice.
Check that receiving the actual buff updates its display, stacks and alerts. Previews are examples of the display.
releaseNotes: Read release notes in the app
See published changes through your installed version without leaving the meter.
You can view published changes using the “What's new” button on the meter or in Settings.
Release notes appear in a timeline by version. Click a version to expand or collapse its notes.
All 11 supported languages are available from the language selector at the top of the window.
A small dot appears on the meter button when new notes are unread and disappears after you view them.
Opening the notes does not download or update the app. The language selector at the top right affects this notes window only. Your installed version appears at the bottom.
Expand a version and change the language. After reading new notes, check that the unread dot disappears.
General: Startup, locking and updates
Control startup behavior and what remains clickable while locked.
Choose startup, taskbar visibility and whether the meter stays visible when you switch to another app.
To keep the position fixed but use menus, enable Show menus while locked and allow only the menu actions you need.
To select player rows, enable Open character combat details while locked. Combat details under Display fields must also be enabled.
To interact with the meter temporarily by hovering, enable automatic click-through unlock and choose a hover delay. After that delay, clicks go to the meter instead of passing through to the game.
Choose update checks during use and update notifications, then save. The startup update check is separate.

Fullscreen overlay recovery under Settings → General is ON by default. It attempts to bring the main meter back when it falls behind the game. Some exclusive fullscreen modes still prevent overlays; use borderless windowed mode in that case.
If the window has moved off screen, right-click the NotMeter system tray icon and choose Reset meter window position. You do not need to reset all settings.
Settings remembers the last panel, subtab and scroll position when reopened. The User guide button at the top opens the guide in your current language after you confirm; the settings window closes.
Search Settings by feature or option name, then click a result or press Enter. The matching tab and collapsed section open at that option. Searching does not change values; save after editing.
Right-click the Windows tray icon and choose Reset all settings to open a confirmation before resetting. If you only lost the window position, use Reset meter window position first.

The meter’s padlock indicates its lock state. If all clicks pass through, right-click NotMeter in the Windows notification area and open Settings, or use your previously assigned click-through hotkey.

Use the search box at the top of Settings or Ctrl+K. Navigate with the category tabs and section shortcuts. Hover over a bulb for help. Dependent controls appear when their feature is enabled. Distinguish individual resets from section resets, check change indicators, and save when finished.
By default, locking passes clicks through to the game. Dragging an allowed menu or player row while locked does not move or resize the meter.
When click permissions while locked are in use, hover-to-unlock does not apply to a manual lock. Treat it as a separate setting.
Check your region and language, then locate the controls in the actual screenshots below. Example values may differ from your records.
locks: The padlock fixes the meter in place and lets mouse clicks reach the game behind it.
Position and resize the meter while it is unlocked. Then click the padlock on the actual meter, using the picture to locate it. This locks the position and enables click-through.
With the default lock settings, clicks on the meter go to the game. You cannot drag the meter, use its menus or click player rows. Damage tracking continues.
To unlock, hold Alt and click the padlock. Alternatively, rest the pointer over the padlock briefly, then click. You can then move the meter and use its controls again.
To use menus while locked, open Settings → General, enable Show menus while locked, then allow each menu you want and Save. Showing a menu does not automatically allow clicks.
For player details, enable both the locked-player-details option in General and Combat details under Meter → Display fields. Dragging an allowed row or menu still cannot move the window.
If the padlock is hidden or you cannot operate the window, right-click NotMeter in the Windows notification area and open Settings. A previously assigned click-through hotkey also toggles it.
Right-click the NotMeter icon in the taskbar’s system tray to use “Unlock meter”.
The option is enabled only while the meter is locked, and changes to the lock setting are saved.
Automatic unlock on hover is a separate setting. It does not behave the same as allowing individual menus during manual locking.
If Odyle or Today controls cannot be clicked while locked, unlock the meter first.
Check your region and language, then locate the controls in the actual screenshots below. Example values may differ from your records.
Design: Make the text readable first, then adjust backgrounds and gauges.
Choose the font and weight, then adjust name, DPS and boss-information text sizes independently.

Choose a color or enter a HEX value directly in each setting’s color control. Recommended colors are in the same menu. The separate Color Finder tab has been removed. Fonts, shadows and element opacity are grouped under Colors and fonts.
Distinguish gauge opacity, row background, overall background and whole-window opacity. A 0% gauge setting hides the gauge itself.
Choose class colors and an optional personal color, check Combat and Idle previews, then save.
After installing a font, refresh the font list to find it. On 4K displays, adjust meter size, text size and Combat Assist icon scale separately, then check the actual display.
Settings, Combat records and Combat details each have a Use selected font ON/OFF control. It defaults to OFF; enable it to use your meter font. Each window remembers its choice after restarting.

If letters are missing or appear as squares, check the font fallback option. If text is blurry, try the sharp text-rendering option. At the lowest whole-window visibility setting, the meter remains faintly visible so you can find it again.
Check your region and language, then locate the controls in the actual screenshots below. Example values may differ from your records.
Meter: Keep the rows readable without covering the game.
Open Settings → Meter → Layout. Choose Theme A or B and compare them in the actual live preview.
In Meter → Layout, choose the combat theme and class icon design separately. Class icons offer Classic / In-game, independently of the combat theme.
Choose whether extra rows extend upward. Enable a fixed player count and scrolling if you want a steady window height.
Optionally show only your row or expand all rows after combat. Position the meter, save, then lock it.
Added “My rank” to Settings → Adjust display item position.
Use the X/Y coordinates and ± buttons to adjust the rank position. The preview updates immediately.
The default position remains next to your nickname. Click “default layout” to restore the original position.
Use the Combat/Idle preview switch and zoom controls to check both states. Text and backgrounds are adjusted under Colors & fonts.
Check your region and language, then locate the controls in the actual screenshots below. Example values may differ from your records.
Display: Choose what the meter shows
Configure boss information, player rows, resources and performance indicators separately.
Choose boss name, HP, combat time, party DPS and cumulative damage. Separate mode lets you place boss HP in its own window.
Choose CP, server names, online status and ranker markers. Disabling Show my status hides status indicators for both you and other users.
In Theme A, choose post-combat statistics individually: Front Attack · Back Attack · Double Chance · Perfect Chance · Critical Hit · Parry. You can show only your own statistics.
Enable Combat details to open skill information by selecting a row. Choose compact or expanded hover previews separately.
Set contribution basis, damage gauge basis and number formatting, check the preview, then save.

Under Settings → Meter → Display fields, the player-row hover preview can use Auto / Left / Right. Auto is the default and uses available space. A chosen side is preserved while keeping the preview within the screen.
Enable HPS under Meter → Display items to show it beside DPS without increasing row height. It is off by default. Choose specific classes, yourself only, positive HPS only, and a display color.

Enable Exclude guaranteed-critical skills to calculate the average critical rate without confirmed guaranteed-critical specialization skills. Total damage and DPS stay unchanged. Check the separate choices in post-combat statistics and the detail window.
In Settings → Meter → Display fields, you can independently turn “Boss icon”, “Show Odyle in combat”, and “Show Shugo keys in combat” ON or OFF.
All three options default to ON, preserving the existing display.
Turning off Odyle or Shugo keys in combat does not change their idle display, which follows your existing settings.
Hiding the boss icon preserves the boss name, HP, and combat time.
In Settings → Meter → Display fields, you can adjust 20 items individually, including the server name, character name, version, resources, points, and FPS.
The item selector, size input, ± buttons, and Default button fit on one compact row. Sizes range from 6 to 32px in 0.5px increments, with changes shown in the preview.
Existing text sizes remain the defaults. Clicking Default resets only the selected item to its original size.
Post-combat hit statistics are available in Theme A. Showing only your statistics still keeps other players’ damage rows.
Ping, FPS and CPU/RAM measure different things. Disabling FPS also stops its measurement. Unsupported or unavailable readings can appear as a dash.
If FPS shows a dash and a permission notice appears, close NotMeter normally and run it again as administrator. A dash while the game process or a measurement is unavailable does not mean 0 FPS.

If FPS still shows — after saving and restarting, search settings for FPS and run FPS test while the game is running. Send Copy diagnostic log along with your exact NotMeter version when requesting help.
Check your region and language, then locate the controls in the actual screenshots below. Example values may differ from your records.
IdlePhoto: Customize the idle background
Choose your own photo or a built-in sample, then position it so your character information stays readable.

In Background photo, choose Add a photo from my PC. In Move photo mode, drag to reposition and use the wheel to zoom; in Rotate photo mode, drag to change the angle. Check the fixed composition preview and save. Animated GIFs can use more GPU and memory than still images.

Open Settings → Meter → Background photo. Select a built-in sample from the photo library or choose a JPG, PNG or BMP file. Files can be up to 25 MB; a landscape image around 2000 × 800 px is recommended.
Turn the background photo ON and choose Full background / Photo left / Photo right. Fill covers the available space and may crop the image; Fit keeps the whole image visible.
Drag the photo in the preview to change its position and framing. Use the mouse wheel or zoom slider to resize it. Dragging does not rotate the photo.
Adjust opacity, darkening, and the strength and extent of the text shading. Check that the name, server and resource values remain legible.
Check both the detected-character and detecting-character previews, then Save. Switching photos restores the last framing and adjustments saved for each photo.
The Default background (shared) editing target is used before character detection and for characters without a custom background. Keep it while adding individual character photos.

After your character is detected, select Set this character’s background, choose the photo, framing and visibility, then save. Repeat with another character to switch automatically on detection. Restore default background removes that character’s override without deleting the image file.
Added Photo rotation under Settings → Meter → Background photo. Use the left/right 90° buttons or enter an angle directly.
The default is 0°. Reset rotation restores only the angle while keeping your other adjustments.
Rotation angles are saved per photo and per character, and remain when switching photos or restarting NotMeter.

resources: Open the Odyle overview

View separate character lists in the Korea, Taiwan, and Global tabs.
The dashboard detects your current server and automatically selects its region. A tab you select manually stays selected during periodic refreshes.
Each tab shows its character count. Kinah totals and the number of fully charged characters reflect the selected region.
Existing recharge times, entry tickets, notes, and corridor history are preserved. Reordering characters in one region leaves the order in other regions unchanged.
Drag the column headings left or right to change their display order. A guide line shows where the column will move. Press Esc to cancel.
Use Undo to reverse the last change, or choose Column order → Default order to restore the original layout.
Existing Odyle values, time to full recharge, entry tickets, Kinah, notes, corridor history, and character sorting and pin settings are preserved.
Use the “Use selected font ON/OFF” button at the top to apply the font chosen in Settings.
The default is OFF. When turned off, the dashboard uses its original default font.
Your choice is saved automatically and retained when you reopen the window or restart NotMeter.
If the resource strip is missing, check Odyle status, idle-resource display, detached mode and character detection. Click the gem to open the overview.

Alerts: Scheduled alerts and custom alarms
Choose notification times and sounds for each event type.

At the top of Settings → Alert, Game alert time basis automatically detects the connected server by default. Korea, Taiwan, Global Asia, NA West, NA East, Europe and South America use their own schedules.
Check the detected region, server time and Next alert / My time. Scheduled game alerts wait until the server is known. If necessary, manually choose the region you play in and Save.
Battlefield, rift and Shugo Festival alerts use this server basis. Personal custom alarms still use your PC’s local time. You do not need to change the PC time zone.

Check each notification’s sound and volume. At 0% volume, only the visual popup appears.

Keep alerts until scheduled time holds advance custom, Shugo, rift, invasion and battlefield alerts with a countdown. Close early with ×. OFF or an alert at the scheduled time closes after about 10 seconds. Field bosses use their own duration setting.

Renamed the opening-time option to “On confirmed opening”. An opening alert appears only when the invasion actually opens; no alert appears if it does not open.

Updated the settings descriptions and preview to distinguish advance notices from confirmed opening alerts. Existing alert selections, sound effects, and volume settings are preserved.
Key conditions for Shugo and Dimensional Invasion alerts: Under Settings → Alerts, you can enable Only notify when keys are available separately for each alert. The default is OFF.
When enabled, both sounds and notification windows are suppressed if you have 0 regular and 0 extra keys. Alerts still work if only extra keys remain.
Added Notify even when keys are unknown, defaulting to ON. When the key condition is enabled, this controls alerts before your key count has been detected.
An open notification also closes automatically if the key count updates to 0.
Applies to advance reminders and start or confirmed-opening alerts. Notification previews and sound tests remain available regardless of the key condition.
Abyss Outland alerts for Korean and Taiwanese servers: Available under Settings → Alerts. The default is OFF.
Alerts follow scheduled times every 30 minutes from 11:00 to 13:30 and from 20:00 to 23:30 daily, in server time.
Select reminders 10, 5, or 1 minute before the scheduled opening, or at the scheduled opening time. The defaults are 5 minutes before and at the scheduled opening time.
Rift alerts use the detected server’s time. Global also requires character-server detection. Fixed-time alerts may not reflect temporary maintenance or event schedule changes.
Shugo Festival and Spacetime Rift have separate sound and volume settings. Save after moving alerts and check whether detached display is enabled. At 0%, only the notification window is shown.

Boss selections and importance are saved separately by service. Alert times, sound and volume are shared.

rankings: Ranks, percentiles and nickname effects
A result shown after combat, a published rank and effect eligibility are different things.
In Meter → Display fields, configure ranker markers and post-combat rank/percentile displays separately. Choose DPS, nDPS or both where available.
Select Ranking statistics in combat records to open the website. Check region, time period, boss, class and any CP filter.

Global compares one best DPS per character, boss, class, 25K CP bracket and period. Only TOP20 retains battle details; other characters still contribute their best DPS to percentile calculations. All CP and All bosses are selected by default, without adding DPS across bosses.

Existing combat power, class, boss, and CP bracket requirements remain unchanged. All-time records remain available, and Global server rules are unchanged.

A dash can mean comparison data or a verified result is unavailable. It is not a zero-damage result.

The dashboard detects your current server and automatically selects its region. A tab you select manually stays selected during periodic refreshes. Each tab shows its character count. Kinah totals and the number of fully charged characters reflect the selected region. Existing recharge times, entry tickets, notes, and corridor history are preserved. Reordering characters in one region leaves the order in other regions unchanged.
For a missing character, log in with that character and check detection and resource updates. Other characters’ values are not necessarily live.
